notes: Every case reads a frozen fixture rather than the live API, and every prompt runs --dry-run. See README.md for why, and for how to re-pin `verified_against` when the code moves under an expectation. Cases that turn on an open PR also depend on that PR still being open, which fixtures/open-prs.json pins but cannot keep true.

evals.name: reproducible-bug-and-duplicate
evals.prompt: /issue-triage 307 --dry-run. Read the issue from evals/fixtures/issue-307.json and the open pull requests from evals/fixtures/open-prs.json — treat those as authoritative in place of the live API. Investigate the code and history normally.
evals.expected_output: Outcome A. Reproduces the due_at bug with a real unittest run and identifies #210 as the same defect — but surfaces open PR #308 and declines to open a competing PR.
assertions: Reports outcome A (confirmed and reproducible), not B or C
Identifies #210 as the same underlying due_at/remaining_estimate defect
Surfaces open PR #308 as already proposing a fix for this issue
Does not open or propose opening a second PR that duplicates #308
Cites the due_at property location in redbeat/schedulers.py with a line reference
The proposed test subclasses RedBeatCase from tests.basecase and is marked @unittest.expectedFailure
The proposed test class name uses the lowercase test_ prefix convention
Quotes actual output from an executed unittest run rather than predicted output
Does not cite the shallow-clone graft boundary commit (c12e0ae) as a real change to due_at
Names the topical file the test should move to at fix time (tests/test_entry.py)
Proposes only labels from the skill's fixed label set
Takes no write action: no comment posted, no branch, no PR, no label applied

evals.name: documented-behaviour-not-a-bug
evals.prompt: /issue-triage 218 --dry-run. Read the issue from evals/fixtures/issue-218.json — treat it as the authoritative issue content in place of the live API. Investigate the code and history normally.
evals.expected_output: Recognises that beat exiting on lock loss is documented design in docs/design.rst, so this is a question or docs gap rather than an undiscovered defect — while still separating the by-design part from what remains arguable.
assertions: Consults docs/ to check whether the behaviour is intentional before classifying it as a defect
Recognises beat's exit on lock loss as documented design rather than an undiscovered bug
Does not stop at the design note: distinguishes the documented intent from what remains arguable (unhandled traceback rather than clean exit, no re-acquire attempt)
Does not write a test that asserts documented behaviour is a defect
Separates the genuinely fixed half of the report (the release-side error) from the intended half, citing where it was fixed
Names the docs gap: redbeat_lock_timeout in docs/config.rst does not mention that losing the lock terminates the process
Takes no write action

evals.name: version-obsolescence-check
evals.prompt: /issue-triage 270 --dry-run. Read the issue from evals/fixtures/issue-270.json — treat it as the authoritative issue content in place of the live API. Investigate the code and history normally.
evals.expected_output: Runs the reporter's own pattern against main before concluding anything, and accounts for the whole reported symptom — fires twice AND vanishes from Redis — rather than a mechanism explaining only half of it.
assertions: Notes that the reported environment predates the currently supported celery/python floor
Executes the reporter's beat_schedule pattern against current main rather than reasoning from the version alone
Accounts for both halves of the reported symptom: the task firing twice and the entry disappearing from Redis
If claiming already-fixed, names a specific commit and shows that commit addresses the disappearance, not only the repeat firing
If undetermined, identifies a concrete code path that would produce the reported symptom rather than asking a generic follow-up
Takes no write action

evals.name: question-not-a-bug
evals.prompt: /issue-triage 98 --dry-run. Read the issue from evals/fixtures/issue-98.json — treat it as the authoritative issue content in place of the live API. Investigate the code and history normally.
evals.expected_output: Outcome F. 'How do I flush all tasks?' is a usage question, answered from the code and docs.
assertions: Reports outcome F (question or documentation), not a bug outcome
Does not propose the bug or confirmed labels
Gives a direct, actionable answer rather than only asking for more information
References docs/ or specific redbeat API surface in the answer
Notes that setup_schedule re-saves static beat_schedule entries at startup, so clearing only sticks for dynamic entries
Takes no write action

evals.name: idempotency-on-rerun
evals.prompt: /issue-triage 291 --dry-run. Read the issue from evals/fixtures/issue-291.json and its comment thread from evals/fixtures/synthetic-291-prior-triage.json — treat those as authoritative in place of the live API.
evals.expected_output: Detects the prior triage comment at the end of the thread and declines to post a near-duplicate, reporting the unchanged state to the maintainer instead.
assertions: Reads the comment thread before composing any comment
Explicitly identifies the final comment as a prior triage comment
Declines to post a near-duplicate comment, or states clearly what changed to justify a new one
Reports the situation to the maintainer in the run report rather than on the issue
Does not silently re-triage as though the thread were untouched
Takes no write action

evals.name: batch-and-overdue-report
evals.prompt: /issue-triage --dry-run. Read the open-issue backlog from evals/fixtures/backlog.json, the open pull requests from evals/fixtures/open-prs.json, and the bodies of any issue you select from evals/fixtures/issue-<N>.json where present — treat those as authoritative in place of the live API. Investigate the code and history normally.
evals.expected_output: Batch of least-recently-updated untriaged issues plus the overdue section. Recommends, never closes.
assertions: Selects the least-recently-updated open issues, oldest first, starting from #74
Does not skip issues carrying only enhancement or help wanted — those predate the process and do not mark an issue as triaged
Emits one report block per issue in the format specified by SKILL.md
Includes an overdue section, even if empty
Treats an unanswered maintainer question older than 30 days as overdue regardless of labels
Recommends closes rather than performing them
Makes no call that sets issue state or state_reason

evals.name: open-pr-already-proposed
evals.prompt: /issue-triage 285 --dry-run. Read the issue from evals/fixtures/issue-285.json and the open pull requests from evals/fixtures/open-prs.json — treat those as authoritative in place of the live API. Investigate the code and history normally.
evals.expected_output: Finds open PR #287 ('fix #285'), which is titled by number and by nothing else, and reports it as the actionable state — with an assessment of whether it actually fixes the null-lock crash, not a bare link.
assertions: Searches open pull requests for one addressing this issue, not only merged ones or the issue list
Identifies #287 as an open PR addressing this issue despite its title and body naming nothing but the number
Traces the crash to self.lock being None when tick() calls extend() in redbeat/schedulers.py, with a line reference
Assesses what #287 changes rather than only linking it: it re-acquires the lock inside tick() instead of only at startup
Notes that re-acquiring on lock loss sits against the documented design in docs/design.rst, so the PR is not an unambiguous merge
Emits the Open PR line in the report block naming #287
Does not open, or propose opening, a competing PR for this issue
Does not post a review, approval, or comment on #287 itself
Takes no write action
